# Vitakkānupatitakathā (Kv 9.7)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vitakkānupatitakathā* (Kv 9.7) is a debate located in the ninth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, the fifth treatise of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The discussion concerns the meaning and scope of the technical expression *vitakkānupatita*, relating to the initial application or direction of the mind (*vitakka*) [Aung & Rhys Davids 1915]. In their translation notes, Shwe Zan Aung and C.A.F. Rhys Davids observe that Burmese translators offered two distinct interpretations of *vitakkānupatita*: either referring to phenomena that constantly accompany the initial application of thought, or to those objects upon which this initial application constantly falls [Aung & Rhys Davids 1915]. These two readings lead respectively to distinct doctrinal inquiries: whether *vitakka* operates in all states of consciousness, or whether it can take all consciousness as its object [Aung & Rhys Davids 1915].
